result.title: When Annotation Patterns Are Learned: Skin-Tone Dependence in Dermatology Concepts
result.summary: Concept bottleneck models (CBMs) let clinicians inspect and correct skin disease diagnoses through clinical concepts, but only if the concept annotations are reliable. We therefore audit the reliability of SkinCon, a widely used dermatology concept dataset, across skin tones. Within the same disease and with near duplicates removed, erythema is annotated far less often on dark than on light skin, with an odds ratio of 0.17. In contrast, hyperpigmentation and hypopigmentation are annotated more often, with odds ratios of 6.2 and 4.5, respectively. We refer to this pattern as tone-dependent concept annotation. An evidential concept model trained on these annotations learns the same pattern and reproduces it on unseen images. Such a model may agree with potential erythema omissions rather than contradict them. Consistent with this, three label error detectors underperform a disease-only baseline at finding erythema that dermatologist captions mention but SkinCon labels as absent. The three detectors are based on confident learning, training dynamics, and the model's own evidential uncertainty. Concept annotations should thus be audited within each subgroup before explanations built on them can be trusted.

AI.brief_summary: 系统审计皮肤科概念数据集 SkinCon 在不同肤色下的标注可靠性，发现在同一疾病内红斑在深色皮肤上被显著少标、色素异常被多标，并检验基于概念训练的模型及三种标签纠错器能否识别这些遗漏。
AI.relevance_reason: 该失败分析提示概念级监督可能内嵌标注偏差，使模型迎合视觉证据的遗漏而非纠正它，对判断「视觉信息是否被真实使用」及解释可信度的监督与评价设计可供核查。
